q: Which part of the neuron receives nerve impulses?
why: Dendrites receive incoming signals from other neurons.

q: The resting potential of a neuron is approximately:
why: At rest the inside of the axon is about -70 mV relative to outside.

why: Impulse jumps between nodes of Ranvier, speeding up conduction.

q: A reflex arc allows a response to occur without involving the:
why: Reflex actions bypass conscious brain processing for speed.

q: Which part of the brain controls heartbeat and breathing rate?
why: Medulla in the hindbrain regulates involuntary vital functions.

q: Which gland is called the 'master gland' of the endocrine system?
why: Pituitary gland controls secretion of many other endocrine glands.

q: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye is the:
why: Retina contains photoreceptor cells that detect light.

q: Which part of the ear is responsible for maintaining balance?
why: Semicircular canals in the inner ear detect body balance and position.

q: At a synapse, the signal is chemically transmitted by:
why: Neurotransmitters released from vesicles cross the synaptic cleft to the next neuron.

q: Depolarization of a neuron's axon membrane is caused by sudden influx of:
why: Opening of Na+ channels lets Na+ rush in, making the inside positive.
